entries.title: Judges 7:1
segments:
Harod; on the borders of Issachar, not far from mount Gilboa. 
 
  Moreh; near the valley of Jezreel. 
 
To obtain the blessings which God has promised, men must not only rely on him, but must employ those means which he has appointed, and in the use of which alone they have reason to expect success.

entries.title: Judges 7:2
segments:
Vaunt; boast. 
 
The means by which, and the manner in which God accomplishes the purposes of his grace, are adapted to show men that the glory of their successes belongs not to them, but to him.

entries.title: Judges 7:3
segments: Mount Gilead; the range of mountains usually so called was on the east of Jordan, but some have supposed that there might be an eminence called by this name on the west of Jordan, where Gideon was.

entries.title: Judges 7:5
segments: Lappeth of the water; from his hand, having raised it to his mouth.

entries.title: Judges 7:7
segments: The power of God's visible people depends not so much on their number as on their character; and sometimes a diminution of their number may give them increased strength.

entries.title: Judges 7:8
segments: The valley; the valley of Jezreel.

entries.title: Judges 7:10
segments: When God has a work for any one to accomplish, he will prepare him to perform it.

entries.title: Judges 7:13
segments: Tumbled into the host; it is represented as rolling down from the hill Moreh, where Gideon was, into the valley where were the Midianites, overturning their tents and prostrating all that was in its way.

entries.title: Judges 7:14
segments: This is--the sword of Gideon; meaning, it represents it, showing that the literal meaning of words is often not their true meaning.

entries.title: Judges 7:15
segments:
Worshipped; bowed himself in grateful reverence before God for giving him this encouragement to go down against the Midianites. 
 
If by a dream, or any other means, one is encouraged to obey the revealed will of God, and strengthened for the performance of known duty, he has reason to be grateful and anew to acknowledge and adore God.

entries.title: Judges 7:16
segments: Lamps; torches.  These were often made of pitchwood, which was easily kindled, and gave a brilliant light.

entries.title: Judges 7:18
segments: The agency of God and that of men are both employed in the accomplishment of his designs.  There is therefore no good reason to imagine that there is any inconsistency between them.

entries.title: Judges 7:19
segments: The middle watch; they divided the night into three equal parts called watches.  The Jews afterwards divided it into four.

entries.title: Judges 7:22
segments: Beth-shittah--Tabbath; supposed to be places towards Jordan, which the Midianites must cross to get into their own country.

entries.title: Judges 7:24
segments: Beth-barah; supposed to be the same as Beth-abara,

. It means, a place of passage, and lay on the east side of Jordan where they crossed the river. 
 
  Took the waters; guarded the fording-places where they expected the Midianites would cross.

entries.title: Judges 7:25
segments: The rock Oreb; so called, it is supposed, from the fact of his having been killed upon it.  So with the wine-press.
